date_note: Date is the article's publication day; the article says the transfers took place between 10 and 15 November and a police complaint was registered on 21 November.
title: Navi Mumbai digital-payments bank: Rs 1,56,91,000 sent to other banks from accounts of 215 customers, police say flaw appears exploited
org: Digital-payments bank (name not given), Navi Mumbai
summary: The Free Press Journal reports unauthorized transfers from the accounts of 215 customers of a Navi Mumbai digital-payments bank. An unnamed police officer said the fraud appears to have exploited a technical vulnerability in the bank's payment system. Rs 1,56,91,000 went to other banks through 523 transactions and was refunded to all 215 customers on 17 November.
plain: A Navi Mumbai payments bank refunded 215 customers after unauthorized transfers. An unnamed police officer says a technical flaw in its payment system appears to have been used.
exec: An unnamed police officer says a flaw in a payments bank's system appears to have enabled transfers from 215 customers' accounts; the bank refunded them.

evidence.quote: Initially, around Rs 1.74 crore was moved from the accounts of 215 customers to 322 other accounts within the bank.
Of this, Rs 1.56 crore was subsequently transferred to accounts in other banks through 523 transactions.
Meanwhile, the bank refunded Rs 1,56,91,000 to all 215 affected customers on November 17

validation.note: Only the Free Press Journal article was read; the bank is not named and no bank or police page was found.
